benchmark_name: Historical OCR evaluation framework with Historical Character Preservation Rate (HCPR) and Archaic Insertion Rate (AIR) on 18th-century Russian Civil font texts
humanities_role_explanation: Targets disciplinary competence of diplomatic transcription of historical print for digital humanities corpus creation, including period-specific orthography (HCPR/AIR metrics), rather than using historical text as generic items.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Page/line images of 18th-century Russian books are given to multimodal LLMs, which output text transcriptions; text GT is compared against output. Post-OCR correction also tested with image+OCR text or text only.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Diplomatic transcription (OCR) of 18th-century Russian Civil font pages in single-line, sliding-window and full-page modes; post-OCR correction experiments; historical character preservation and archaic insertion analysis.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task (historical OCR) and one corpus (18th-century Russian Civil font).

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 12 multimodal LLMs: Claude 3.5/3.7, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o4-mini, Gemini 2.0/2.0 Flash-Lite/2.5 Flash/2.5 Pro, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Llama-4 Maverick/Scout.

quantitative_metrics.note: CER, WER, case-insensitive CER/WER, HCPR, AIR, CaseER, coefficient of variation of word accuracy.

summary: The paper presents an evaluation methodology for LLM-based historical OCR with contamination-aware dataset creation, novel metrics (HCPR, AIR), and stability testing, demonstrated on 1,029 pages of 18th-century Russian Civil font books. Twelve multimodal LLMs are compared; Gemini and Qwen models perform best, LLMs 'over-historicize', and post-OCR correction does not help.
key_findings: Gemini-2.5-Pro best in full-page mode (CER 3.36%, WER 4.69%, historical character error 9.83%). Traditional OCR much worse (Tesseract CER 21.55%, PyLaia 26.93%, Surya 45.96%). Models insert archaic characters (GPT-4o in 59% of files). Context-enhanced Russian prompts reduce CER by up to 0.02. Post-OCR correction degrades or fails to improve performance.
facets_explanation: GT was prepared by layout analysis (YOLOv8), initial TrOCR transcription, then 100% manual correction in eScriptorium by a single expert annotator with a two-pass protocol following diplomatic principles. A 500-line stratified sample was audited by a second verifier (98.6% line exact match, 99.93% character accuracy). Scoring compares output to a single transcription via Levenshtein distance.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports Gemini-2.5-Pro full page 'CER (%) 3.36' and WER 4.69. The largest input-mode gap is Gemini-2.5-Flash CER 4.94 (full page) vs 25.63 (sliding window), about 21 points; however GPT-4o 9.23 vs 23.75 single line is ~14.5. Largest: Gemini-2.5-Flash 4.94 vs 25.63 gives 20.69, so see note. No human baseline is given; the 98.6% verifier agreement is a GT audit, not a human-vs-model baseline.

humanities_role.quote: Using 18th-century Russian Civil font texts, we introduce novel metrics including Historical Character Preservation Rate (HCPR) and Archaic Insertion Rate (AIR)

dataset_size.quote: a novel dataset of 1,029 pages from 428 unique 18th-century Russian books

evaluation_set_size.quote: which serves as the evaluation set for the LLMs

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: we tested three prompting strategies: a simple English prompt, a context-enhanced English prompt, and a context-enhanced Russian prompt

gold_source.quote: GT was produced by a single expert annotator using a two-pass protocol.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: preserving period-specific orthography, hyphenation, original errors, typos, and spacing conventions to accurately reflect the source documents

answer_multiplicity.quote: Character Error Rate (CER) and Word Error Rate (WER), using Levenshtein distance between prediction and ground truth.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: We evaluated all models across the three recognition modes using standard metrics
